entries.answer:
[ERROR LIST]

- Line: `PORT` is converted without validation. A nonnumeric value becomes `NaN`, and `server.listen()` throws `RangeError` with code `ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT`; startup terminates.[1][6][370]

- Line [12–13, 198, 304]: Nonnumeric `MAX_BODY_BYTES` or `MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` values become `NaN`. Both limit comparisons then always evaluate to false, silently disabling the corresponding size limit.[1]

- Line: A nonnumeric `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` becomes `NaN`; the page-closing timer receives `NaN` and runs with a 1 ms delay instead of the configured request deadline.[14][240][1]

- Line: Zero or negative `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` values reject every completion request with HTTP 429, even when no request is active. These configurations are not rejected at startup.[16][318][1]

- Line [66–73]: `closeBrowser()` awaits closing the current browser and subsequently clears the shared globals unconditionally. If another operation installs a replacement browser during that await, the replacement browser, context, and authentication-page references are erased.[1]

- Line [76–92, 340–342]: Browser initialization has no shared initialization promise or lock. Concurrent model requests can launch multiple browsers, overwrite the global browser reference, and leave an earlier browser unclosed. Completion serialization does not protect the models endpoint.[1]

- Line [78, 81–91, 126, 134]: The browser becomes globally visible before its context, authentication page, and authentication are ready. A concurrent call can pass the connected-browser check and then throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'newPage')`, or access an authentication page before initialization finishes.[1]

- Line [102–120, 134–138]: Authentication and catalog fetches have no abort signal or application deadline. A fetch or response-body read that remains pending can leave browser initialization or model loading pending indefinitely; the generation-page timer does not cover these operations.[1]

- Line [114–121]: Authentication failures are indiscriminately reported as HTTP 401. For example, an upstream sign-in HTTP 503 becomes `upstream_authentication_error` with status 401, misclassifying an upstream availability failure as an authentication failure.[1]

- Line [139–141]: Catalog HTTP 401/403 responses trigger unbounded recursive retries. If authentication succeeds but catalog access continues returning 403, `loadModels()` never returns a terminal error and repeatedly authenticates and fetches.[1]

- Line : Catalog groups are dereferenced without a null check. A catalog containing `[null]` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'models')` instead of producing a controlled catalog-validation error.[1]

- Line [169, 311–313]: The requested model is coerced before its type is validated. A JSON model value of `{"toString":null}` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`, which becomes HTTP 502 instead of a controlled invalid-request error.[1]

- Line : Exact identifiers and aliases are searched together in catalog order. An earlier model whose name equals a later model's actual ID shadows that ID and selects the wrong model. For example, requesting `"second"` selects `{id:"first",name:"second"}` before `{id:"second",name:"other"}`.[1]

- Line [178–186]: Unsupported content parts are silently discarded. A mixed text-and-image request sends only its text to Arena, without rejecting the unsupported image or telling the client that the submitted input was changed.[1]

- Line [192–196]: Invalid message entries are silently removed rather than rejected. For example, `[null,{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]` is accepted and converted into a prompt after dropping the null entry.[1]

- Line [193–197]: Role labels can satisfy the nonempty-text validation without any message text. `[{"role":"assistant","content":""}]` produces `"assistant:"` and passes the check that claims to require text. Multiple empty user messages also pass because their role labels remain.[1]

- Line [195–196]: Message-role serialization is ambiguous and does not preserve structural role boundaries. A system message `"x"` followed by a user message `"y"` produces exactly the same Arena prompt as one user message containing `"system:\nx\n\nuser:\ny"`.[1]

- Line: Error detection scans ordinary page text for unrestricted phrases. A legitimate prompt or answer containing `"generation failed"`, `"failed to generate"`, or `"something went wrong"` is treated as an upstream generation failure and returns HTTP 502.[217][252][257][1]

- Line [221–229]: Response extraction starts after the earliest model-name substring anywhere in the supplied text, including inside the user's prompt or navigation. For `"User: Explain M\nM\nCorrect answer"`, it returns `"M\nCorrect answer"` rather than isolating the assistant response.[1]

- Line : If extraction cannot find a model label, it returns the entire supplied text instead of rejecting unidentified content. With the body-text fallback, this can return navigation, account text, or other page content as the assistant answer.[1]

- Line [230–235]: Assistant text is truncated when it contains either an exact prompt surrounded by blank lines or `"\n\nInputs are processed"`. These strings are treated as boundaries even when they occur inside a legitimate answer.[1]

- Line [239–240]: `arenaPage()` runs before the generation timer and outside the generation `try` block. Browser initialization, authentication, and page creation therefore have no generation-level deadline and bypass its timeout-error translation.[1]

- Line: For a finite nonnegative `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` below 5000, the page-closing timer fires before the mandatory 10000 ms wait completes. Such configurations cannot reach response inspection successfully.[240][247][1]

- Line [240, 264–265]: The explicit deadline closes the page without recording a timeout error. The resulting page-closed exception falls through to HTTP 502 rather than the HTTP 504 timeout branch.[1]

- Line [250–253]: Completion detection requires the model label to occur after the prompt. A rendered body of `"M\nP\nFinished answer"` with prompt `"P"` never satisfies the predicate, despite containing an answer and no generation marker.[1]

- Line: The completion waiter recognizes only `model.publicName`, while candidate selection and extraction also recognize `displayName` and `name`. A response labeled solely with either supported alternative cannot pass the waiter.[251][254][258][1]

- Line : Completion detection does not require assistant content or an explicit completed-generation state. A body containing only the prompt followed by the model label passes, permitting response extraction before an answer exists.[1]

- Line : `"Generating..."` is searched across the entire page, including the user prompt and assistant answer. A prompt containing that exact string prevents successful completion detection even after generation finishes. Conversely, `"Generating…"` does not block the predicate, so a body containing that status and a partial answer can be returned as finished.[1]

- Line [258–260]: Only the first model-containing candidate is extracted. If that candidate contains just a model header, extraction returns empty and raises HTTP 502 even when a later candidate or the full body contains the actual answer. No alternative candidate is tried.[1]

- Line [272–285]: The returned usage counts are synthetic character-length estimates, not measured model-token counts or upstream usage. They are placed directly in `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, and `total_tokens` without identifying them as estimates.[1]

- Line: `finish_reason` is hard-coded to `"stop"` without observing the upstream termination reason. Partial content accepted by the completion predicate is therefore also reported as normally finished.[284][294][1]

- Line [289–296, 330–337]: Streaming is simulated after complete generation. The entire assistant response is buffered and then emitted in one content event; `stream: true` does not stream generation as it happens.[1]

- Line: The heartbeat interval is ineffective. It is created and cleared in the same synchronous function invocation, so its callback cannot execute and no keep-alive is sent while generation is pending.[291][295][1]

- Line [311–313, 330–335]: Completion controls other than `model`, `messages`, and the exact boolean `stream` are silently ignored. Requests specifying `n`, token limits, stop sequences, sampling controls, tools, or response-format constraints receive neither enforcement nor an unsupported-option error. For example, `n: 2` still produces one choice, and a requested stop sequence is left in the response.[1]

- Line : Invalid `stream` types are silently interpreted as false. For example, `"stream":"true"` is accepted but produces a nonstreaming response instead of a validation error.[1]

- Line [317–322]: The promise chain serializes every completion regardless of a positive concurrency setting. With `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=3`, actual concurrency remains one. Because the previous task decrements `activeRequests` before the next task checks it, the overload check never rejects competing requests for a positive limit.[1]

- Line [328–330, 317–323]: The waiting queue has no size limit or waiting deadline, and each queued closure retains its parsed request payload. Additional requests accumulate rather than receiving the advertised concurrency-limit error; a permanently pending task blocks every later completion.[1]

- Line [326–337]: Client disconnection does not cancel queued or active work. There is no request/response close handling to remove abandoned tasks or stop their browser generation, so abandoned requests continue consuming the serialized processing slot.[1]

- Line: Catalog entries are deduplicated by Arena ID, but the models endpoint exposes `publicName` as its model ID. Two distinct Arena IDs with the same public name produce duplicate external IDs; requesting that shared ID resolves only the first matching model.[151][343][1]

- Line : Every model's `created` field is the hard-coded placeholder timestamp `0`; no creation timestamp is obtained from the catalog.[1]

- Line [351, 359–360]: An invalid Host value such as `":"` makes URL construction throw `TypeError: Invalid URL`. The generic error handler reports this client-input parsing failure as HTTP 502 `upstream_error`.[1]

- Line [364–365]: The HTTP timeout assignments do not establish a response-processing deadline. Once the request body has arrived, queue waiting, authentication, and catalog loading can continue beyond `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` without these server settings terminating the operation.[1]

- Line [367–368]: Shutdown closes the browser before stopping acceptance of new HTTP requests and does not mark the application as shutting down. New or already queued requests can consequently start browser initialization again during shutdown; pending work is neither cancelled nor prevented from reopening the browser.[1]

[END OF LIST]
